question: do the doubler valleys kill the current of a polarised 1s? (hypothesis of phase 2, sec. 12.8)
argument_before_runs: Phase 2 found: net two-tick flux = F1(psi) - F1(Theta W2 psi) for ANY psi (identity from the exact time reversal; checked again on a 4^3 random-potential lattice: 5e-17), and F1(psi) = F1(Theta psi) inside ONE Kramers doublet, so every stationary state has zero net flux. This does NOT cover combinations of different doublets: two doublets on the same colour give net flux 0.31 (check), and the old E5 state (2 doublets, split 3e-4) circulated (0.23). A valley-k=0 state is a combination of the 4 doublets of the 1s quartet; with the learned nucleus the quartet is split by ~2e-4 (beat ~6e4 ticks), so the state is quasi-stationary over 4000 ticks AND is allowed to carry current. The test can work; it is run.

setup.lattice: Walk3D 48^3, a = theta = 0.5 lambda_C, Z = 60 (Za = 0.4378), point nucleus on the corner of 8 cells

nuclei.learned: NUCLEO_1S sec. 13 (learn2): Coulomb potential x 0.554593 on the 8 cells at r0 = sqrt3/2 a, x 1.003549 on the 24 cells at r1 = sqrt11/2 a (2 + 6 per colour); everything else -Za/r

setup.preparation: seed = radial Dirac 1s (kappa = -1, m = +1/2) on the cube; listening pass 1: 2048 ticks, Hann, candidates 0.86..0.94 step 0.0025, peak of the autocorrelation spectrum; pass 2: 2048 ticks at the peak from the pass-1 state; then projection P0 on valley k = 0 (Fourier cells nearest to k = 0 or its pi copies, the same valley_split as phase 2), normalised. The same recipe for both nuclei.
setup.run: 4000 ticks, 2e5 exact surfers (S4-2 two-tick flow, Pollock), Born start; records every 100 ticks: fidelity |<psi0|psi(t)>|^2, valley-0 weight, <Sigma_z>, flux v_phi of the state, z of the surfers (2^3 blocks); surfer v_phi over 10-tick windows starting at 500, 1000, 2000, 3000, 3990, measured exactly as E5 (v_phi = r_c dphi / (10 a), divided by sin = r_c/r, mean over 1 < r < 6, |z| < 0.5 r, divided by Za).

F1.what: learned: the prepared state is a polarised k = 0 electron: valley-0 weight >= 0.99 and <Sigma_z> >= 0.9

F2.what: (a) learned: quasi-stationary: fidelity >= 0.9 and valley-0 weight >= 0.9 at every record up to 4000

F3.what: (b) learned: surfers rotate like Bohm-Dirac: v_phi/(Za sin) in [0.75, 1.25] in all 5 windows

F4.what: learned: surfers stay |psi|^2: max |z| <= 4 over the run

F5.what: (c) bare control behaves differently: valley-0 weight < 0.5 at some record OR surfer v_phi outside [0.75, 1.25] in at least 2 of the 5 windows (prediction of the doubler hypothesis)

F6.what: learned: flux v_phi of the state at t = 0 in [0.75, 1.25] (the current is in the state, not made by the surfers)

note: If F2-F4 and F6 pass while F5 passes too, the hypothesis 'the doublers kill the current' is supported: removing the valley mixing (learned nucleus) and starting in k = 0 gives the Dirac rotation. The learned nucleus is NOT removing the doublers, only their mixing: the state is still a combination of 4 lattice doublets.
